point: Fodstad et al. name four open challenges in energy modelling: resolution, uncertainty, multi-energy systems and transition dynamics.
Prina et al. find the key challenge is reaching high resolution in all dimensions at the same time.
Models must be transparent for policy use, because hidden assumptions prevent informed decisions.
Coarse spatial resolution misstates renewable shares and results, especially when renewables are high and regionally varied.
Models used for Bolivia differ in aims, and none achieves high resolution in every category.
Dispa-SET has been used for Bolivian studies and offers detailed techno-economics but only medium time and space resolution.
OSeMOSYS has served Bolivian policy studies and couples sectors well but has coarse time resolution.
The LUT model has produced Bolivian pathways and is detailed in most dimensions except techno-economics and transparency.
PyPSA-Earth-BO is open-source with fine time resolution, medium spatial and techno-economic detail, and electricity only.
Bolivia's electricity relies on gas that is running down, so diversifying toward renewables is urgent.
Costly gas and oil subsidies plus limited reserves and decarbonisation pressure argue for reducing fossil dependence.
Studying Bolivian transition paths under subsidies needs a transparent investment model, and earlier work points to data and model improvements.
The study improves transmission data, grid investment, spatial detail, hydropower expansion and constraints.
The study gives a view of Bolivian transition pathways to 2040 with and without fuel subsidies.
The study shows economic and technical effects of pathways to help policymakers judge subsidy reform.
The paper's remaining sections cover method, data, scenarios, results and conclusions.
Few energy models treat input uncertainty even though it strongly affects results, and reviews agree handling it is a priority.
Stochastic programming handles uncertainty but is computationally heavy and covers few parameters, so modellers must pick key parameters and state assumptions.
Stochastic programming grows in importance because deterministic models understate costs and emissions and overstate variable renewable contribution.
No open-source Bolivian model handles uncertainty, and the proprietary one in use is not open.
The open-source Bolivian models are all deterministic, so uncertainty in open-source planning is an unexplored gap.
EMPIRE is an open-source multi-horizon stochastic model that could be adapted beyond Europe but has only been used there.
The study implements EMPIRE for Bolivia to compare stochastic multi-horizon planning with deterministic single-period planning.
A fragment names a deterministic model with load flow optimisation as the comparison.
Because models need approximations, the comparison will weigh the strengths and weaknesses of each model's assumptions.
The rest of the paper covers methods, data adaptation, validation, comparison and conclusions.
